item.text: {"search_note":"For 2B.8, the best-supported reading is that military spending and mobilization were clearly tied to real threats, while procurement was opaque, with large lump-sum equipment spending and limited disclosure of what was bought. I found no direct evidence that Tinubu used defence spending to intimidate neighbors or reward a patronage network, but the lack of disclosure means I also cannot rule that out cleanly.","evidence":[{"title":"President Tinubu’s 2024 Budget Presentation at the Joint Session of the National Assembly, Abuja","publisher":"State House, Abuja","date":"November 29, 2023","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-2024-budget-presentation-at-the-joint-session-of-the-national-assembly-abuja/","summary":"Tinubu said defence and internal security were top priorities in the 2024 budget and that the internal security architecture would be overhauled to protect lives, property, and investment. This is the strongest negative item for 2B.8 on opacity: the scale is large, and the procurement is not fully transparent.","question_ids":["2B.8","2B.3"]},{"title":"FG acquired N32bn weapons, others for military in 2024 – Report","publisher":"Punch","date":"February 16, 2025","url":"https://punchng.com/fg-acquired-n32bn-weapons-others-for-military-in-2024-report/","summary":"The report said the Ministry of Defence disbursed over N33bn in July 2024 for “critical and urgent operational equipment,” but the specific equipment and intended use were not disclosed.
